scope: development-only complementarity audit for a recall-anchored dual-expert successor
motivation: The frozen Stanford controlled-release evaluations showed that the released MARS detector retained high-rate sensitivity that the stronger ERSRR scene rankers lost. This audit asks whether that released-detector signal is complementary on authorized MARS folds 3/4 before any new architecture is fitted.

allowed: descriptive failure analysis on already-opened folds 3 and 4
forbidden: threshold selection for external or official test data
opening or rescoring any official, Stanford, UNEP, EMIT, MethaneS2CM, or CloudSEN outcome

scores.current_v3: released_primary_scores in the champion cache; historical field name retained for hash compatibility

fixed_analysis.matched_fpr_comparator: >= threshold chosen independently for each score at no more than 0.0713 negative FPR
fixed_analysis.feature_contrast: standardized mean difference between released-paper-rule rescue true positives and rescue false positives

continue_to_recall_anchored_architecture: the released detector recovers at least one champion-missed positive
the released-only region contains both positives and negatives so a verifier has a nontrivial task
at least one frozen model-aligned feature has an absolute standardized contrast of at least 0.25
decision_rule.otherwise: retire released-detector rescue before model fitting
